# Summing individual convex-potential certificates

This note proves a quantitative combination rule for a **fixed finite collection** of actual regular critical-circuit boundary profiles. It also computes its exact optimum on the planar sharp product example and a strictly paying constant test on a genuinely oblique, globally critical three-fiber example. It does not prove that every individual circuit admits the required efficiency, nor identify the number of profiles with an arithmetic parity count.

## 1. The finite summation rule

Let `eta` be a finite nonzero Borel measure on a compact physical subset of Euclidean space. Let `W_1,...,W_N` be fixed, nonnegative, bounded Borel functions. Let `C` be a cone of nonnegative continuous convex functions, closed under sums and positive scalar multiples. Suppose for each `i` there is `Phi_i in C` with

    integral Phi_i d eta=1,
    integral Phi_i W_i d eta>=gamma_i>0.            (1)

Then the single function

    Phi=sum_i Phi_i/gamma_i

satisfies, simultaneously for all `i`,

    integral Phi W_i d eta / integral Phi d eta
        >= (sum_j 1/gamma_j)^(-1).                 (2)

In particular `gamma_i=Gamma` gives `Gamma/N`.

Proof: the denominator is `sum 1/gamma_j`. Nonnegativity gives
`integral Phi W_i >= (1/gamma_i) integral Phi_i W_i >=1`. No disjointness or common exposed face is needed. All functions and measures here are the same in every integral.

An attained optimum is unnecessary. If the individual suprema over positive-denominator tests are at least `Gamma`, then for any `epsilon>0` choose normalized tests with efficiency at least `Gamma-epsilon`. Their sum has all efficiencies at least `(Gamma-epsilon)/N`. This suffices for every strict target below `Gamma/N` without an unproved compactness assertion for the test class.

The rule also permits a finite overlap matrix. Given normalized tests `Phi_j`, set `A_ij=integral Phi_j W_i d eta`. Every probability vector `a` produces the common efficiency vector `Aa` via `sum a_j Phi_j`. Thus the exact best efficiency supplied by those tests is the finite linear program

    max_(a_j>=0,sum a_j=1) min_i sum_j A_ij a_j.     (3)

This retains favorable cross-profile contributions; (2) only uses the diagonal ones.

## 2. Exact interface with regular critical covers

In the positive-fiber setting let `eta` be the sum of ordinary boundary measures of the actual fibers. It is finite. For a fixed regular positive critical circuit group `i`, write

    W_i=sum_j theta_ij 1_(H_ij),
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_l rho_il/S_il),
    rho_ij>0,  sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0.

Here `u_ij` is the continuous normal, `S_ij>0` is the actual coarea section measure, and the caps have the same raw mass. Regularity includes the threshold differentiability used in the displayed formula and zero `eta`-mass on the cap boundaries. Hence `0<=W_i<=1` with no supporting-facet allocation hidden in the notation.

The actual compatible erosion defined by a nonnegative global convex potential has regular group response

    beta integral Phi d eta - integral Phi W_i d eta,          (4)

where `beta` is the original normalized common cap mass. Thus (2), if its individual hypotheses are established, makes every response in (4) strictly negative when `beta<(sum 1/gamma_i)^(-1)`. Turning this into a decrease of the global depth also requires that the selected reoptimized circuits and the retained slack covers control every actual fiber. These geometric hypotheses are not consequences of the sum identity.

In particular, `N` is the number of selected profiles. The sum lemma alone gives **no** bound `N<=k` in terms of occupied parities. The archived fixed-parity-face-witness theorem does prove a fixed selection of `s<=k(I)<=k(P)` deepest-base witnesses such that one arbitrarily selected critical circuit at each witness covers all deepest fiber planes. Thus `N=s` is justified when each witness admits a circuit satisfying the present regular-profile hypotheses and the archived quantile-persistence conditions. This is a separate geometric theorem, not an implication of (1). In particular its cardinality conclusion is not being left as an unproved claim here; the individual quantitative premise and regularity/allocation interface remain the obligations. Grouping several profiles of one parity also needs justification. If a group is replaced by an average of its old profiles, its individual efficiency can change; a union of cap lists is not automatically one regular positive circuit with the old normalized weights.

Similarly, if positive supporting-facet mass is present, the actual stress profiles can contain allocated traces rather than closed indicators, with dependent section weights. The elementary sum rule remains true for any *fixed* nonnegative profiles, but a universal individual-efficiency assertion must cover the allocations produced by the actual stress theorem. It is not enough to optimize an independently convenient allocation for each test. No such nonsmooth extension is claimed here.

The admissibility of sums is genuine for the global potential class: if `m(z,x)` is the concave signed fiber margin, then `{m>=epsilon Phi}` is convex for every convex `Phi`; replacing finitely many potentials by their sum stays in this class. The quantitative payment and the circuit-count interface are separate from this elementary admissibility fact.

## 3. A one-dimensional convex-order identity on a triangle edge

Define on `[0,1]`

    w(t)=1/3+(1/3)1_[1/3,2/3](t).

For every continuous convex `f`,

    integral_0^1 f(t) w(t) dt <= (4/9) integral_0^1 f(t) dt.    (5)

Indeed, for `0<=t<=1/3`, convexity gives

    2 f(t+1/3)<=f(t)+f(t+2/3).

Integrating yields `3 integral_(1/3)^(2/3) f <= integral_0^1 f`, which is exactly (5). This proof works even if `f` changes sign. For nonnegative `f` it compares the corresponding positive weighted measures directly. Equality holds for affine `f`; no equality characterization is needed below.

## 4. Exact optimum on the sharp binary-times-triangle family

Let `T={(x,y):x,y>=0,x+y<=1}` and `P={0,1}^n`, with `n>=0`. Let `S=P times T`, the actual intersection induced by `[0,1]^n times T`. Put `N=|P|=2^n`.

Use barycentric functions `lambda_0=1-x-y,lambda_1=x,lambda_2=y`. For `p in P`, define the affine base function

    L_p(z)=sum_l [(1-p_l)z_l+p_l(1-z_l)].

On the binary bases it is the Hamming distance to `p`. The three ambient caps

    H_(p,j)={lambda_j(x)-1/3-L_p(z)>=0}             (6)

strictly miss every other binary fiber and are the three centroid vertex caps on fiber `p`. All have raw area `2/9`. Their continuous normals sum to zero and all normalized sections have length `2/3`, so their response weights are exactly `1/3`. Their sections have common full ambient centroid `(p,1/3,1/3)`.

These are genuine globally critical circuits. At each displayed source every containing halfspace captures at least `2/9` from its own triangle by the ordinary triangle centroid inequality (a pure-integer cap contains that whole fiber). Conversely the three caps (6) cover the entire `p`-fiber and each has raw mass `2/9`, for every `p`. Thus the global raw depth is `2/9`. All other fiber traces of (6) are strictly empty, so the regularity and boundary-null premises of Section 2 hold.

Let `W_p` be the profile from (6), extended as zero on all other fiber boundaries. On each of the three edges of its own triangle, the barycentric edge parameter makes it exactly the function `w` in Section 3. Consequently every global nonnegative continuous convex potential satisfies

    integral Phi W_p d eta <= (4/9) integral_(boundary T_p) Phi d eta.  (7)

The edge lengths, including the diagonal edge's factor `sqrt(2)`, multiply both sides of (5) and cause no normalization change. Summing (7) over `p` proves

    min_p integral Phi W_p d eta / integral Phi d eta <= 4/(9N).       (8)

Thus no global convex potential can beat the claimed common factor on this actual sharp family.

It is attained. The base hinge

    phi_p(z,x)=(1-L_p(z))_+

is a global nonnegative convex function, equals one on fiber `p`, and vanishes on every other measured fiber. If `B=perimeter(T)=2+sqrt(2)`, then `Phi_p=phi_p/B` has denominator one and individual efficiency exactly `4/9`. Moreover the sum of the unnormalized hinges is one at every measured base. Formula (2) therefore attains equality in (8). In particular the individual best efficiency is exactly `4/9`, and the common best is exactly `4/(9N)`.

This is a proof for the entire convex-potential cone, not just a numerical test over hinges. It also illustrates why the continuous coordinates alone cannot substitute for base localization when there are several groups.

Even on the one-triangle case, two tempting margin potentials lose a fixed amount. For the unscaled critical margins,

    Phi_max=max_j (lambda_j-1/3)_+,
    Phi_sum=sum_j (lambda_j-1/3)_+,

the exact efficiencies are respectively `2/5` and `5/12`, both below `4/9`. On each edge, `Phi_max=max(t,1-t)-1/3` has total integral `5/12` and middle-third integral `1/12`. The sum potential has the corresponding integrals `4/9` and `1/9`. Inserting these in `w` proves the stated ratios. Thus simply taking the maximum or sum of actual critical margins does not supply the individual sharp constant; here the constant potential does.

## 5. A strictly paying test for an actual oblique three-fiber circuit

Use the already independently certified globally critical example in `candidate c0a17a15efbe8efa`:

    h=20/97, t=100/291, e=1/100,
    K_z={x,y>=0, h<=x+y<=1+ez},      z=-1,0,1,
    Y=(0,t,t),        s=3t-1.

The actual full convex body is defined by these four continuous inequalities and `-1<=z<=1`. The three caps are

    H1: x+y<=2t,
    H2: t x+s y-e t z>=t(4t-1),
    H3: s x+t y-e t z>=t(4t-1).                    (9)

The cited proof certifies their common raw mass `Q=3[2t(1-2t)]` as the global maximum against every ambient orientation. Here we compute a new boundary-potential coefficient, rather than infer criticality from stationarity.

The continuous circuit coefficients are `(4t-1,1,1)`. Each `H1` coarea section has normalized length `2t`; each `H2,H3` section has normalized length two. Thus the total coarea measures are `(6t,6,6)` and

    theta1=(4t-1)/(6t-1),  theta2=theta3=t/(6t-1).  (10)

Their section centroids are all exactly `Y`: the `H1` section center is `(t,t)` in each fiber, the `H2` center is `(t+ez,t)`, and the `H3` center is `(t,t+ez)`, with symmetric base weights. Every cut is proper on every fiber. It intersects each boundary in finitely many points, so the boundary profile is regular.

Let `W=sum theta_j 1_(H_j)`. On the outer diagonal edge of each fiber the two nonempty captured edge lengths, after removing the common `sqrt(2)` factor, are both `2t`. On the inner edge the only nonempty trace is the whole `H1` trace. On either coordinate-axis edge, the `H1` trace has length `2t-h`, one of `H2,H3` has length `2-4t`, and the other is empty. Since `sum_z(1+ez)=3`, direct integration gives

    eta(total)=3[(2+sqrt(2))+(sqrt(2)-2)h],
    integral W d eta
      =3[4(2+sqrt(2))t^2+(sqrt(2)-2)h(4t-1)]/(6t-1).          (11)

Therefore the constant normalized potential `Phi=1/eta(total)` has efficiency strictly larger than `4/9`. To check the strict sign exactly, subtract `(4/9)eta(total)` from the numerator in (11) and multiply by the positive `(6t-1)/3`. The result is

    4(2+sqrt(2))(t-1/3)^2
      +(sqrt(2)-2)h(4t/3-5/9).                     (12)

Here `1/3<t=100/291<5/12`, `h>0`, and `sqrt(2)-2<0`, so both terms in (12) are strictly positive. No numerical evaluation or surrogate fiber sum is used.

Thus the individual criterion succeeds on a genuinely oblique critical menu with three unequal, nonhomothetic fibers and strict no-heavy volume. The example does not prove the criterion for other bodies. In particular, neither this calibration nor the summation identity removes the two remaining obligations: an individual quantitative efficiency theorem on the actual allowed profiles, and the regularity or allocation-aware extension needed to use the proved arithmetic witness selection.

## 6. Exact normal-dependent radial-hinge identity and its obstruction

This section uses the normal-bundle version of `eta`: a boundary point of a full-dimensional convex fiber is marked by its outward unit normal, defined at boundary-almost-every point. Let `d>=1`, let the positive fibers be `K_p`, and let their total volume be `M`. Fix a source `Y=(p0,c)` and any affine continuous center field

    f_p=c+A(p-p0).

Define the signed radial velocity and its two nonnegative parts by

    V0(p,x,n)=n.(x-f_p),
    V=(V0)_+,              Xi=(-V0)_+.             (18)

The function `V` is a nonnegative continuous normal-dependent potential, convex in physical coordinates for each fixed normal. It is an admissible normal-bundle erosion velocity. Directly, each fixed-normal inequality

    n.x+epsilon[n.(x-f_p)]_+ <= h_p(n)

has a convex left side and a concave right side in the base variable, and their intersection is convex. At almost every regular boundary point its inward first velocity is `V`. Alternatively the normal-bundle approximation by a partition of unity in `n` reduces it uniformly to nonnegative sums of admissible physical affine hinges.

Let a finite family of caps through `Y` be

    H_j={a_j.p+v_j.x>=b_j},          v_j!=0,

with the same raw mass `Q`. Assume their cuts are regular, their boundaries have zero `eta`-mass, and their full mixed section measures have centroid exactly `Y`:

    sum_p sigma_jp p = S_j p0,
    sum_p integral_(K_p intersect boundary H_j) x dH_(d-1)/||v_j||
       = S_j c,
    sigma_jp=H_(d-1)(K_p intersect boundary H_j)/||v_j||,
    S_j=sum_p sigma_jp>0.                           (19)

Proper, strictly empty and strictly full cuts are allowed. Positive supporting-facet allocations are not incorporated into this particular formula.

For any convex combination `W=sum_j theta_j 1_(H_j)`, the exact identities are

    integral V0 d eta=dM,
    integral V0 W d eta=dQ.                         (20)

The first is the divergence theorem in each actual fiber applied to `x-f_p`. For the second, apply that theorem to each proper cap. Its cutting section has outward normal `-v_j/||v_j||`. Therefore

    integral_(boundary K_p intersect H_j) n.(x-f_p) dH_(d-1)
       = d |K_p intersect H_j|
          +(b_j-a_j.p-v_j.f_p) sigma_jp.            (21)

The same identity holds for strictly empty or full cuts, with zero section term. Summing the correction in (21) and using (19) gives

    sum_p (b_j-a_j.p-v_j.f_p) sigma_jp
       = S_j[b_j-a_j.p0-v_j.c]=0,

since the cap passes through `Y`. Averaging the common `dQ` values proves (20). Thus every integer-coordinate and affine-center contribution has been retained and canceled by an explicit section-centroid hypothesis, not discarded by replacing a fiber sum by an integral.

For genuine regular depth-attaining caps, (19) follows from unrestricted normal first variations at the fixed source: differentiating a cap with normal increment `(delta a,delta v)` gives the coarea integral of `(delta a,delta v).(p-p0,x-c)`. It vanishes in every direction at a minimum. This derivation requires the stated differentiability; (19) is also an explicit independently checkable hypothesis of the result.

Since `V=V0+Xi`, (20) gives the exact nonnegative-hinge efficiency

    integral V W d eta / integral V d eta
       = [dQ+integral Xi W d eta]/[dM+integral Xi d eta].       (22)

The denominator is at least `dM>0`. In particular the hinge's surplus above `beta=Q/M` is

    [integral Xi(W-beta) d eta]/[dM+integral Xi d eta].         (23)

This formula exposes the precise extra credit needed when an affine center field leaves other fibers. If all its centers lie inside their fibers then `Xi=0` and the efficiency is exactly `beta`, regardless of the affine field.

There is an exact actual obstruction to promoting this class to the individual `Gamma_d` premise. Use Section 4's binary-times-triangle example with `N>=2`, one source `p0=p`, and its individual profile `W_p`. On that source fiber, `f_p=c` is its interior centroid; hence `V0>0` on its entire boundary and `Xi=0` there. On every other fiber `W_p=0`. It follows that

    integral Xi W_p d eta=0

for **every** affine matrix `A`. Formula (22) consequently gives

    efficiency(V;W_p) <= Q/M = 4/(9N) < 4/9.        (24)

Equality is attained by `A=0`, since the constant field is the common interior triangle centroid on every fiber. Every nonnegative finite sum of such matching-source radial hinges also has efficiency at most `4/(9N)`, by summing numerator and denominator inequalities. Thus the entire proposed radial-hinge cone fails the individual sharp efficiency on an actual globally critical example satisfying the common mass and section-centroid conditions.

This does not obstruct the full convex-potential class: the base hinge from Section 4 achieves exactly `4/9` for the same profile. It identifies a concrete need for base localization or another mechanism beyond matching-source radial homothety. The obstruction does not extend to arbitrary normal multipliers or different potential classes without a separate argument.

## 7. Two rigorously reducible easy cases in the plane

For a regular group with `W=sum theta_j 1_(H_j)`, write its signed affine cap margins as `ell_j`, positive on `H_j`'s interior. The actual hinge `Phi=(ell_j)_+` is supported in that cap, so

    integral Phi W / integral Phi >= theta_j.       (25)

Its denominator is positive: the cap is proper on its anchor fiber, with interior source, so an open boundary patch lies strictly on its positive side. The hinge is positive on that patch, which has positive ordinary boundary measure. Thus any weight `theta_j>=4/9` supplies the individual planar target. In particular every two-cap positive circuit is paid, since one of its two weights is at least one half. A remaining three-cap group has

    1/9<theta_j<4/9 for all j.                      (26)

There is another actual geometric escape. Let `C` be the canonical convex hull of its positive fibers. If an exposed point `w` of `C` lies **strictly in two** caps `H_i,H_j`, then one sufficiently shallow exposing affine hinge has its entire measured support in that double intersection. Its efficiency is at least `theta_i+theta_j`, hence exceeds `5/9` under (26).

For completeness, an exposed point of this finite-fiber hull belongs to an actual measured fiber: a convex representation by the finite compact fiber union, together with uniqueness of the exposed maximizer, forces every used point to equal `w`. Choose an exposing functional `L` with unique maximizer `w`. Compactness implies `{L>max_C L-epsilon}` is contained in the strict double intersection for small positive `epsilon`. On its source fiber the boundary near `w` has positive boundary measure, so `(L-max_C L+epsilon)_+` has positive denominator. This proves the assertion without assuming that all extreme points are exposed, or that a zero-measure vertex itself carries surface mass.

Thus the hard balanced three-cap case can be restricted, for this test, to bodies with no exposed point strictly double-captured. This is a proved reduction for the individual-potential test, not a classification of those remaining bodies.

## 8. Base-localized radial hinges and an exact support-function credit

Pure matching-source radial hinges fail in Section 6 because they charge all measured fibers. At an exposed integer base one can localize them exactly, while retaining convexity.

Let `p` be an exposed vertex of the finite base hull. Choose an affine function `L_p` with `L_p(p)=0` and `L_p(q)<0` at every other measured base. Fix any `c in K_p`. For sufficiently large finite `B`, the normal-dependent convex hinge

    V_(p,c)(u,z,x)=[u.(x-c)+B L_p(z)]_+             (27)

vanishes on every other measured fiber boundary, for every unit `u`. Indeed the finitely many strict negative base gaps dominate the uniform bound on `||x-c||`. On its own boundary it equals `u.(x-c)>=0`, since `c in K_p`. Consequently

    integral V_(p,c) d eta=d |K_p|.                 (28)

For one fixed regular cap profile `W=sum theta_j 1_(H_j)`, put

    C_p=sum_j theta_j |K_p intersect H_j|,
    T_p=sum_j theta_j sigma_jp v_j,
    B_p=sum_j theta_j sigma_jp (b_j-a_j.p).

Applying (21) only to this actual fiber gives the exact coefficient

    integral V_(p,c) W d eta = d C_p+B_p-T_p.c.     (29)

Optimizing over the compact body `K_p`, with actual support function `h_Kp`, yields the attained efficiency

    E_p=[d C_p+B_p+h_Kp(-T_p)]/(d |K_p|).           (30)

The point attaining the support maximum belongs to `K_p`, so (27) remains a nonnegative radial velocity on that fiber. The parameter `B` can then be chosen finitely; there is no limiting realization hidden in (30). This is an exact test using actual cap volumes, sections, normals and base position. Unlike a scalar volume certificate it retains one common directional support term. If any exposed base has `E_p>=4/9` in dimension two, the individual planar profile is paid by an admissible potential.

## 9. Three-fiber endpoint support identity

For the complete chain bases `{-1,0,1}`, write the fibers as `A,K,B`, and suppose the source is `(0,y)`. Assume the regular section-centroid conditions (19). Their integer-coordinate part forces

    sigma_j,-=sigma_j,+ = s_j

for every cap. Define

    T=sum_j theta_j s_j v_j,
    C0=sum_j theta_j |K intersect H_j|,
    M0=(A+B)/2.

Since every cap passes through `(0,y)`, `b_j=v_j.y`. The sum of the two attained endpoint numerators from (30) is therefore exactly

    |A| d E_- + |B| d E_+
       = d(Q-C0)+2[T.y+h_M0(-T)].                  (31)

Proof: the endpoint cap terms sum to `Q-C0`, because the original caps have common total mass `Q`. The integer-normal terms cancel between the two endpoints, their remaining `B_p` terms sum to `2T.y`, and the support terms satisfy `h_A(-T)+h_B(-T)=2h_M0(-T)`. This establishes (31) from the same actual shapes and directions.

In particular some endpoint-localized test has efficiency at least

    [d(Q-C0)+2(T.y+h_M0(-T))]/[d(|A|+|B|)].        (32)

The numerator is nonnegative because it is the sum of two actual nonnegative boundary integrals, even if `y` is outside `M0`. If `y in M0`, the displayed support-distance correction is separately nonnegative. No unconditional location of `y` in `M0` is assumed. Equation (31) is an exact directional credit for the proposed individual-efficiency mechanism; whether it reaches `4/9` in other chains remains a separate question. It is not substituted for the missing universal individual theorem.

For the actual oblique example in Section 5, each fiber has the same cap areas `delta=2t(1-2t)` and the same coarea lengths `(2t,2,2)`. Formula (10) gives `T=0`, but the integer-threshold term in (30) is not zero: it is `B_p=4e t^2 p/(6t-1)`. Thus the endpoint test on `A=K_(1-e)` has exact efficiency

    E_-=[delta-2e t^2/(6t-1)]/|A|
       =12368000000/27259241181
       =4/9+758345092/81777723543.                    (33)

This is a second actual paying potential, distinct from the constant one. Choose `c` to be the centroid of `A` and the base exposing function `L(z)=-(z+1)`. The finite potential `[u.(x-c)-4(z+1)]_+` vanishes on the other two fibers: every continuous point and `c` lie in `[0,101/100]^2`, so `||x-c||<2<4`. It has precisely the efficiency (33), by (28)--(30). Thus base localization repairs the pure radial-hinge obstruction in a genuinely oblique example while retaining the exact section and boundary geometry.

Audit correction: an earlier version of (33) incorrectly omitted `B_-` after observing `T=0`. The displayed value now retains that integer-threshold term. The companion checker independently integrates the actual boundary cap traces against the radial normal velocity, as well as checking formula (30). No general identity in (28)--(32) changed.

The equal endpoint section weights in (31) are an arithmetic premise. For three unequally spaced sampled sites `{0,t,1}`, at the middle source the actual stationarity equation instead reads `t sigma_j,0=(1-t) sigma_j,1`. It cannot be replaced by the unweighted equality used here. The archived exact counterexample in `candidate 640d07cd1de2a423` also shows why an unrestricted finite-base efficiency-plus-minimum argument cannot be promoted to the mixed-integer target by replacing lattice completeness with a finite-base Helly number. No such promotion is made by the identities or sufficient tests above.
